Moving to the survalis verb interface

Source: vignettes/from-1.0.Rmd
from-1.0.Rmd

survalis 1.3.0 introduced a seven-verb interface. It keeps every prior function working – nothing you have written breaks. The granular helpers stay exported as the low-level layer under the verbs (see ?survalis-lowlevel). This vignette shows the verb that covers each of them.

The mapping

Granular (still works) Verb interface (recommended)
fit_ranger(f, data, num.trees = 500) fit(f, data, "ranger", spec = list(num.trees = 500))
predict_ranger(m, nd, times) predict(m, nd, times)
predict_*() then survmat_to_rmst() predict(m, nd, times, type = "rmst", tau = ...)
predict_*() then survmat_to_quantile() predict(m, nd, times, type = "median") / type = "quantile"
cv_survlearner(f, data, fit_ranger, predict_ranger, times, folds = 5) evaluate(f, data, "ranger", times = ..., resampling = cv(5))
score_survmodel(m, times, metrics) evaluate(m, times = ..., resampling = cv())
tune_ranger(f, data, times, param_grid, refit_best = TRUE) tune(f, data, "ranger", grid = param_grid, times = ...)
benchmark(f, data, learners, times) compare(f, data, models = learners, times = ...)
best_survlearner(bench, metric) print() a survalis_compare (best is flagged)
compute_pdp(m, data, "karno", times) interpret(m, "pdp", feature = "karno", times = ...)
compute_shap(m, nd, data, times) interpret(m, "shap", newdata = nd, times = ...)
compute_varimp(m, times) interpret(m, "varimp", times = ...)
plot_pdp(res, "karno") plot() a survalis_interpret
estimate_rmst(m, data, tau, times, trt_col = "trt") estimate(f, data, "<model>", treatment = "trt", tau = ...)

Side-by-side 

library(survalis)
f <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype

# 1.x
m1 <- fit_ranger(f, veteran, num.trees = 200)
p1 <- predict_ranger(m1, veteran[1:3, ], times = c(90, 180))

# 2.0
m2 <- fit(f, veteran, "ranger", spec = list(num.trees = 200), seed = 1)
p2 <- predict(m2, veteran[1:3, ], times = c(90, 180))

round(as.matrix(p2), 3)
#>       t=90 t=180
#> [1,] 0.404 0.269
#> [2,] 0.857 0.484
#> [3,] 0.649 0.435

What changed on purpose

  • predict() always returns a survmat for the curve types: an n x length(times) matrix with the grid in attr(x, "times"). The "t=<time>" column names are still there, so the *_survmat() metric helpers keep accepting it.
  • times is optional. When omitted, default_times() builds a grid over the observed event times and records it on the result (res$times), so a run is reproducible.
  • evaluate() / compare() take a resampling object (cv(), holdout(), group_cv(), bootstrap()) instead of a bare folds integer, and compare() evaluates every model on the same folds.
  • fit() engine arguments go in spec, not ....
